subagent_reports.architecture_assessment:
Q1 PASS — Official docs say Signal returns when server accepts it and does not wait for delivery/processing (https://docs.temporal.io/develop/typescript/workflows/message-passing). SDK source only awaits SignalWorkflowExecution RPC (https://github.com/temporalio/sdk-typescript/blob/55e4ad36a99e27c14bedb9326ddf7f7246240353/packages/client/src/workflow-client.ts#L1211-L1236). Thus an open execution may accept a Signal and handle.signal() resolve before its next Workflow Task fails replay with TMPRL1100; catch-gating recovery is structurally wrong. RPC rejection, closed/missing execution, transport, or authorization can still make signal throw.

Q2 PASS with caveat — Query requires a Worker and waits for Worker response (https://docs.temporal.io/develop/typescript/workflows/message-passing); maintainers confirm bad/nondeterministic workflows can return 'Cannot query workflow due to Workflow Task in failed state' or time out (https://community.temporal.io/t/queryworkflow-cannot-query-workflow-for-failed-state/8733). This is not universal across every cache/race, so classify actual errors. Describe directly invokes service RPC (https://github.com/temporalio/sdk-typescript/blob/55e4ad36a99e27c14bedb9326ddf7f7246240353/packages/client/src/workflow-client.ts#L1430-L1443), while server builds it from mutable state without replay (https://github.com/temporalio/temporal/blob/ddce4c204f4746fb2c945bcc40932f2139cd2016/service/history/api/describeworkflow/api.go#L63-L280). Nondeterminism alone should not block describe, though service/persistence failures can.

Q3 FAIL — pendingWorkflowTask contains state, attempt, and timestamps, but no Workflow Task last failure/cause/TMPRL1100 text (https://typescript.temporal.io/api/interfaces/proto.temporal.api.workflow.v1.IPendingWorkflowTaskInfo). pendingActivity.lastFailure is unrelated (https://typescript.temporal.io/api/interfaces/proto.temporal.api.workflow.v1.IPendingActivityInfo). Nondeterministic Workflow Task failure leaves execution open/RUNNING and task retrying (https://docs.temporal.io/tasks). RUNNING plus pending/retried task can also mean timeout, worker crash, infrastructure trouble, or another Workflow Task failure; describe cannot reliably classify poison. Current regex over describe JSON therefore has no standard field from which to find TMPRL1100 (file:///home/jon/dev/advance/plugin/src/tools/recovery-probe.ts#L23-L123). Exact evidence should come from captured errors or WorkflowTaskFailed history failure/cause (https://docs.temporal.io/references/events#workflowtaskfailed; https://typescript.temporal.io/api/interfaces/proto.temporal.api.history.v1.IWorkflowTaskFailedEventAttributes).

Q4 CAUTION — Temporal's canonical repair is Reset after fixing code, with post-reset-point progress discarded (https://docs.temporal.io/develop/typescript/workflows/cancellation#reset-a-workflow-execution). Prevention uses patched()/deprecatePatch(), Worker Versioning, and replay testing (https://docs.temporal.io/develop/typescript/workflows/versioning; https://docs.temporal.io/production-deployment/worker-deployments/worker-versioning; https://docs.temporal.io/develop/safe-deployments). Disk projection is an application break-glass bypass, not Temporal healing. It can be reasonable for terminal ADV bookkeeping only with explicit authorization, exact evidence, idempotent writes, durable divergence warning, and prompt terminalization/archive.

Overall — Pre-signal branching is necessary, but describe-only poison classification is unsound. Use describe for run/existence/status/closed-state binding. For RUNNING poison recovery, require precise captured TMPRL1100 provenance or inspect WorkflowTaskFailed Event History before writing projection without signaling.

blockers: DescribeWorkflowExecution lacks Workflow Task failure cause/text and cannot reliably establish that a RUNNING workflow is poisoned. Authorizing disk mutation from pendingWorkflowTask/status/attempt or regex over standard describe output risks bypassing a healthy-but-delayed workflow.
validation.notes: Per-question verdicts: Q1 PASS; Q2 PASS with race/cache caveat; Q3 FAIL; Q4 CAUTION. Design becomes sound after separating describe's liveness/closure role from poison authorization.

tradeoffs: Pre-signal recovery fixes reachability but creates split authority between Temporal and disk projection.
History inspection gives authoritative evidence but adds bounded fetch/parsing complexity.
Reset preserves Temporal authority but forks a run and discards later progress.
Operator-supplied TMPRL1100 evidence is simpler but weaker without durable provenance.
Versioning and patching prevent recurrence but add deployment lifecycle overhead and do not repair existing poison.

## Problem
Poisoned-history recovery for ADV change-workflows is structurally unreachable (3 confirmed facets: catch-gated-behind-fire-and-forget-signal, target_path routes recovery to the dead Temporal store, acceptance readiness reads a projection the recovery never writes). Stranded gates cannot be safely completed.

## Objective
Make `recoveryMode:"poisoned_history"` recovery deterministically reach the disk projection and unblock stranded gates, without weakening the audit/evidence gate, and prove it heals a real poisoned change (pokeedge-web `fixWorktreeViteCache`).

## Scope
- **Probe-before-signal**: when `recoveryMode:"poisoned_history"` is set, `describe()`-probe the workflow for poisoned/completed evidence BEFORE firing any signal; take the disk-direct recovery branch directly instead of relying on a signal throw. Apply uniformly across `gate.ts` (gate completion), `verification-evidence.ts`, `task.ts`, `design-concern.ts`, `contract.ts`.
- **target_path recovery routing**: ensure poisoned_history recovery under `target_path` writes the target's disk projection (the same projection reads/readiness consume), not the poisoned Temporal store.
- **Readiness/projection consistency**: acceptance/release readiness must read the projection that recovery writes, so a recorded verification-evidence disposition actually clears its `VERIFICATION_EVIDENCE_MISSING` blocker.

## Acceptance criteria
- With a poisoned (unreachable) workflow and `recoveryMode:"poisoned_history"` + full audit args, `adv_verification_evidence_disposition` records the disposition to the disk projection and a subsequent readiness check no longer reports that gap — no signal timeout, no false success.
- `adv_gate_complete` acceptance/release poisoned recovery completes from the disk projection when upstream gates + contract + evidence are present, without a 30s poll timeout.
- The same holds under `target_path` routing (untrusted target, explicit confirmation).
- Regression test reproduces the fire-and-forget-signal-does-not-throw case and asserts the recovery branch is reached (no reliance on the signal throwing).
- Ends by healing pokeedge-web `fixWorktreeViteCache` acceptance as the live proof.

## Constraints / avoidances
- Do NOT weaken the recovery evidence gate (recoveryEvidence must still be precise poisoned/completed evidence; audit fields still required).
- Do NOT auto-terminate, reset, or reseed healthy workflows; poisoned classification stays witness-first.
- Prevention (Temporal Worker Versioning / deploy-safe worker rollover) is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE — tracked separately as P2.
documents.problemStatement:
ADV change-workflows poison recurrently with TMPRL1100 patch-marker nondeterminism after an ADV worker-bundle redeploy (no Temporal Worker Versioning; deploy-local.sh SIGKILLs the worker mid-replay). When a workflow is poisoned, the typed poisoned_history recovery paths that are supposed to heal stranded gates are **structurally unreachable**, leaving changes stuck with no safe operator lever — most visibly at the acceptance gate.

Confirmed live this session against pokeedge-web change `fixWorktreeViteCache` (acceptance pending, all upstream gates done, contract READY, executive summary persisted):

1. **Catch-gated recovery.** `adv_gate_complete`, `adv_verification_evidence_disposition`, `adv_task_update`, `adv_design_concern_disposition`, and `adv_contract_*` fire the workflow signal FIRST and only run the disk-direct recovery inside a `catch`. Temporal signals are fire-and-forget (`_adapters.ts` fireSignal) — they return success even when the poisoned workflow cannot replay — so the `catch` never fires. Control falls through to a 30s poll (`waitForGateCompletion`) that times out with a generic "not confirmed"/"stuck" error. The recovery branch is never entered.

2. **target_path projection split.** Under `target_path` routing, poisoned_history recovery mutations route through the Temporal target store (`stateMode:"temporal"`) — i.e. a buffered signal to the dead workflow — instead of a disk-projection write. `adv_verification_evidence_disposition` returned `success:true` twice yet nothing landed.

3. **Readiness/projection mismatch.** Acceptance readiness re-derives from the disk projection (`stateMode:"disk-snapshot"`, `_recovery.reason:"poisoned_history"`), which never sees the temporal-store writes, so `VERIFICATION_EVIDENCE_MISSING` blockers persist permanently.

Impact: high-volume projects (pokeedge 123 changes, pokeedge-web 155 changes) accumulate many parked change-workflows that outlive each plugin redeploy, so poisoning — and unrecoverable stranding — recurs. The observable symptom is an agent reporting "poisoned Temporal history … no safe reset tool is exposed here," which is operationally accurate even though the recovery tools nominally exist.

# Executive Summary

## Outcome
ADV's poisoned-workflow recovery is now deterministic and disk-authoritative across 6 catch-gated tools plus the archive path. Operators can heal a wedged change via precise evidence without depending on a Temporal signal throw, and the 3 most material describe()-only authority bypasses have been closed. Release-ready: production-readiness scan passed, cleanup 0 candidates, pre-existing issues tracked as follow-up.

## Why It Matters
The previous catch-gated pattern relied on the signal RPC itself failing — but Temporal signals are fire-and-forget (server-acceptance returns, not workflow-processing). On a poisoned workflow the signal silently resolves and the recovery branch was unreachable, leaving operators stuck. This change ships a probe-first authority model (`shouldTakeRecoveryBranch`) that trusts operator-supplied precise evidence UPFRONT, before the signal fires, and writes the disk projection directly. The C2 remediation (PR #275) additionally closes 3 describe()-only authority paths that violated the agreement. The wedge class — workflow poisoned mid-flight, signal silently drops, recovery unreachable — is structurally resolved.
